title: Validating an autoclave cycle for a biohazardous waste load
summary: Prepare a typical waste load, place thermocouples and biological indicators, run a steam cycle, incubate and read the indicators with a positive control, and report whether the cycle is validated and what exposure time the load needs.
scenario: Your laboratory must validate the autoclave cycle it uses for bags of solid BSL-2 waste. You have a typical load, autoclave bags, leak-proof trays, thermocouples, self-contained biological indicators and an incubator. The indicator lot's D-value is printed on its label.
guided_steps: Bag the waste and close the bag loosely so steam can enter; place it in a leak-proof tray; do not exceed the chamber's rated load.
Place a thermocouple and a biological indicator at the centre of the load, the slowest point to heat, and others at the top and near the drain.
Keep one indicator from the same lot unprocessed as a positive control.
Run the cycle at 121 °C with an exposure long enough for the centre: its heating lag plus twelve D-values.
Record the cycle's time, temperature and pressure in the autoclave log.
Incubate the processed indicators and the control at 55–60 °C for at least 24 h, then read them.
The cycle passes only if the control grows and no processed indicator grows. Report the centre lag and the validated exposure time.

checkpoints.description: Close autoclave bags loosely so steam can enter.
checkpoints.rationale: A sealed bag traps air, and the centre never reaches steam temperature.

source.location: Appendix A, Part 5, p. 386: 'The bag should be loosely closed (to allow steam to enter the bag)'

checkpoints.description: Autoclave bags in a leak-proof tray or pan.
checkpoints.rationale: Bags can leak or split during the cycle.

source.location: Appendix A, Part 5, p. 387: 'The bag should be transported and autoclaved in a leak-proof tray or pan'

checkpoints.description: Do not exceed the chamber's rated load.
checkpoints.rationale: Overloading blocks steam circulation and lengthens heating.

checkpoints.description: Place a thermocouple at the centre of the load.
checkpoints.rationale: Validation must show that steam reaches the slowest point.

source.location: Appendix B, Decontamination: 'thermocouples and biological indicators (BIs) placed throughout the load'

checkpoints.description: Place a biological indicator at the centre of the load.
checkpoints.rationale: The centre is the hardest place to sterilize, so it decides the cycle.

checkpoints.description: Incubate an unprocessed indicator from the same lot as a positive control.
checkpoints.rationale: Without a growing control, a 'no growth' result could mean dead indicators or a failed incubator.

checkpoints.description: Run an exposure of at least the centre lag plus twelve D-values at 121 °C.
checkpoints.rationale: Exposure counts only once the slowest point reaches temperature.

source.location: Appendix B: cycle times for high-bioburden waste 'should be verified and validated for the typical load'

checkpoints.description: Incubate indicators at 55–60 °C for at least 24 h.
checkpoints.rationale: Spores that survive need the right conditions to grow and show the failure.

checkpoints.description: Record the cycle's time, temperature and pressure.
checkpoints.rationale: Routine monitoring of cycles is part of verification.

source.location: Appendix B: 'routine monitoring of the steam sterilization cycles (i.e., cycle times, pressure, temperature)'

checkpoints.description: Report the centre heating lag measured by the thermocouple.
checkpoints.rationale: The lag sets the minimum cycle for this load.

checkpoints.description: Report 'validated' only if the control grows and no processed indicator grows.
checkpoints.rationale: Any growth, or a control that fails to grow, means the cycle is not shown to work.

checkpoints.description: Set the exposure for this load at no less than the lag plus twelve D-values.
checkpoints.rationale: A shorter routine cycle would leave the centre under-treated.

sources.use: Bagging, tray, thermocouple and indicator placement, 121 °C, and routine cycle monitoring, adapted from a US federal government work.

limitations: Heating lag and indicator D-values come from a simple model; real loads are validated by measurement for each load type.
Survival is modelled as first-order kill once the centre reaches temperature; heating and cooling ramps are ignored.
Chamber capacity and indicator incubation conditions are practice values; follow the autoclave and indicator manufacturers' instructions and your institution's procedures.
